title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
hints: you get to invent the string format yourself - the only requirement is that your deserialize function can perfectly undo whatever your serialize function did

a preorder traversal (node, then left, then right) that also emits an explicit marker for every missing child contains enough information to rebuild the exact tree shape, unlike a traversal that omits missing children
pick a delimiter that can never be confused with a real value or the missing-child marker, for example a comma, and join node values (or the marker) into one string in preorder order

to deserialize, split the string back into tokens and consume them in the same preorder order: read one token as the current node's value (or stop if it's the missing-child marker), then recursively build the left subtree, then the right subtree, from the remaining tokens
reuse a single 'position in the token list' cursor across the whole recursive deserialize call, since each recursive call must pick up exactly where the previous one left off
commonMistakes: omitting markers for missing children, which loses shape information and makes deserialization ambiguous (e.g. can't tell a lone left child from a lone right child)
using a delimiter or missing-child marker that could also appear as part of a real negative number's string form, causing a parsing collision
trying to deserialize with an index passed by value through recursive calls instead of a shared, mutable cursor, so sibling subtrees don't see how many tokens the previous subtree consumed
using level-order (BFS) serialization but forgetting that every present node still needs both of its child slots represented, even at the last level

content.problemStatement:
Binary trees in these problems are encoded as a flat array named `tree` using complete-binary-tree (heap) indexing:

- the root sits at index 0
- a node at index `i` has its left child at index `2*i+1` and right child at index `2*i+2`
- a child index only counts as real if it's within the array's bounds **and** its value isn't the sentinel `-101`
- `-101` means "no node there" - real node values are always in the range -100 to 100, so -101 can never be mistaken for a genuine value

**Design a way to serialize a binary tree into a string and deserialize it back into the same tree, then, given a tree in the flat array encoding, serialize it and immediately deserialize the result, returning the reconstructed tree in the same flat array encoding.**

There's no constraint on the string format other than that your serialize and deserialize functions must agree with each other. A correct solution always returns exactly the tree it started with, structurally identical down to which children are present.
constraints: the input array is always a valid, minimal flat encoding (its last element is never the sentinel, unless the whole tree is empty)
notes: a tree containing negative values and zero, which must be distinguishable from the sentinel and from each other in your string format
a deeply skewed tree (every node has only one child), which stresses how your format handles long runs of missing children

optimal.time: O(n) to serialize and O(n) to deserialize, each visiting every node (and every missing-child marker) once
optimal.space: O(n) for the string representation, plus O(h) recursion stack
optimal.pattern: preorder DFS serialization: emit the current node's value, then recursively serialize left, then right, using a distinct marker for missing children

bruteForce.approach: there isn't really a slower alternative here - any correct serialize/deserialize pair takes linear time; the interesting choice is the encoding scheme, not an asymptotic tradeoff. a naive scheme like a level-order (BFS) string with explicit null markers works but produces a longer string than a compact preorder scheme

bruteForce.space: O(n) for the string and the rebuilt tree
